Subject: CedarBridge: deployment channel qualification & isolation expectations

Hi Sarah / Alex — thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we keep momentum: 

- Summary of CedarBridge preference we heard: tenant-level isolation (no shared inference tenancy), control plane scoped to your VPC or customer-managed control plane, and CMEK for model keys.
- Questions we flagged on the call: whether you require on-prem air-gapped deployment for any workloads, and whether logs/metrics need to remain in your AWS account or a Redwood-managed store is acceptable.

Requested evidence / quick asks from CedarBridge so we can map to a deployment lane:
1) Confirmation if multi-tenant GPUs are strictly prohibited for any PHI workloads.
2) Which KMS provider must hold keys (AWS KMS customer keys, HSM, other).
3) Scope of network egress restrictions (IP allowlist, private-peering only, no internet egress).

We can cover these on a 30-minute follow-up (we're proposing Mon 4 Aug at 10am PT). In parallel, I'm looping in Aditya (inference infra) and Marcus (eng ops) to start a short evidence bundle: SOC 2 summary, a reference architecture for Private (VPC) control plane, and the Dedicated capacity operational playbook.

Next steps: 
- You reply to confirm the three asks above and the call time.
- Redwood will share the evidence bundle and a one-page decision checklist comparing Dedicated vs Private for your security/cost tradeoffs.

Thanks — Laura

Laura — thanks for the recap and for taking notes. A few clarifications from our side:

- For PHI workloads we cannot accept shared GPU tenancy. All PHI inference must run in an environment where compute is not shared between tenants (we prefer single-tenant Dedicated or fully provisioned Private nodes).
- Control plane: CedarBridge requires control-plane management to be in our VPC (Private control plane). We cannot hand control-plane administrative access to a third-party-managed control plane for production PHI.
- Keys: we prefer AWS KMS customer-managed CMKs; HSM is acceptable if needed.
- Logs/Telemetry: metrics can be forwarded to CedarBridge S3/CloudWatch, but full trace-level request logs must remain in our account for at least 1 year.

We can do Mon 4 Aug 10am PT. I will bring our security architect. Also please share SOC 2 summary and a brief network diagram before the call so our security team can pre-scan.

Best,
Sarah Cole
Head of Platform
CedarBridge Health

Sarah — great, thanks for the clarifications and confirming the 4 Aug slot. Per your asks, attached are the items Aditya and Marcus prepared; see the highlights below before the call.

Attachments (short stubs):
- redwood-soc2-summary.pdf — one-page SOC 2 scope + control map (we call out which controls cover tenant isolation and access reviews).
- private-deploy-architecture.png — conceptual diagram showing Private control plane in customer VPC + optional on-prem connector.
- dedicated-capacity-ops-playbook.pdf — how Dedicated pools are provisioned, tenancy guarantees, patching windows, and audit evidence path.

Quick mapping (high level):
- If PHI requires strict single-tenant compute and control plane residency in your VPC, Private (customer-managed control plane in your VPC with customer network egress rules) is the tightest fit. It supports CMEK and keeps control-plane metadata in your account.
- Dedicated capacity (Redwood-managed control plane + dedicated GPUs reserved for you) gives single-tenant compute but the control plane is still Redwood-hosted; we provide strong separation and SOC 2 backed controls, and we can arrange customer-managed keys for data at rest. For teams that need minimal operational lift but still require compute isolation, Dedicated is often chosen.

Pre-call ask for CedarBridge security team to review: the three attachments + the one-page decision checklist (link below). We'll come prepared with a proposed PoC scope: 2-week Private control-plane sandbox or 2-week Dedicated pool evaluation (your choice).

Decision checklist (short link): https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/cedarbridge-poc-plan

Thanks — Laura

Laura / Marcus — internal notes to prepare for Mon call and to draft a POC BOM: 

- Private control plane options: we can offer (A) customer-managed control-plane in their VPC (our control-plane binaries run in their account via an operator) or (B) fully air-gapped on-prem; A is already supported in our private stack and is fastest to stand up (expected 3–5 business days for a sandbox with limited scale).
- Dedicated: single-tenant GPUs, but control plane remains Redwood-hosted. For PHI path with CedarBridge constraints, we can offer Dedicated + CMEK + strict egress controls to route telemetry to CedarBridge. This reduces time-to-eval (1–2 days for a small dedicated pool) but needs contractual clarity about control-plane admin access.
- Evidence to pull for the call: SOC 2 summary, network diagram for customer-managed control plane, sample IAM roles we provision, list of KMS integration patterns, sample SLA for Dedicated.

I'll be on the 4 Aug call. Will prepare a short BOM and a sketch of timeline for both PoC options.

Sarah / Alex — thanks again. Confirmed items and next steps before our 4 Aug call: 

1) Evidence bundle shared (see attachments). Please share any initial feedback before Mon so we can update the PoC materials.
2) Two PoC lanes to choose from: 
   - Private control-plane sandbox (in your VPC): full control-plane residency, CMEK support, no shared control-plane metadata outside your account. Estimated sandbox time: 3–5 business days to stand up, 2-week validation window.
   - Dedicated capacity evaluation: single-tenant GPUs reserved for CedarBridge, Redwood-managed control plane. Fastest to start (1–2 days), lower operational overhead, can be combined with CMEK. Note: we will need to document admin responsibilities for the control plane in the contract.

3) Pre-call homework for CedarBridge security: confirm KMS preference (AWS CMK or HSM) and note any mandatory IP egress constraints.

4) Action owners: 
   - CedarBridge: confirm KMS and any hard egress constraints (Sarah).
   - Redwood: Aditya to deliver PoC BOM and timeline; Marcus to pull sample IAM roles and audit trace examples; Laura to own scheduling and contract questions.
